title: Wickedly Predicting the Unintended Consequences of Decisions
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece proposes a "wicked reflection" exercise for stress-testing decisions before they are finalized. Using examples ranging from Airbnb's effect on housing to the psychological toll of the social media "Like" button, it illustrates how well-intentioned decisions can produce serious unforeseen harm. The recommended technique asks decision-makers to imagine how the most self-interested or malicious actor could exploit or misuse a choice, surfacing risks before they materialize. The article acknowledges unintended consequences can never be fully eliminated, but argues this kind of adversarial thinking meaningfully reduces the odds of being blindsided.
points: Introduces a devil's-advocate technique called "wicked reflection" for anticipating harm
Uses real examples (Airbnb, the social media Like button) to illustrate unforeseen consequences
Provides specific probing questions leaders can ask before finalizing a decision
Acknowledges the limits of the technique while still advocating for its regular use
quotes: For leaders, the devil isn’t in the details. It’s in the unintended consequences of the decisions they make.
Known as “blowback” in clandestine operations, the unforeseen outcomes of a decision can cause a big mess and turn a straightforward decision into a disaster.
An inventor of the “Like” button on social media doesn’t anticipate the effects of receiving or not receiving likes will have on teenager self-esteem.
The best leaders put every critical decision to a wicked test before fully embracing it.
By identifying the worst “use” of a decision, leaders can construct strategies to offset or mollify negative outcomes.
Without the test of wicked reflection, leaders go blindly into a future of unintended consequences.
